text.p: Boeing Commercial Airplane Group said on Thursday it has accelerated plans to boost Boeing 737 production in response to increased demand for the jet.
The Boeing Co. unit said the twinjet will be produced at a rate of 17 airplanes a month by the third quarter of 1997, six months ahead of the schedule announced in June.

The 737, which is currently produced at a rate of 8.5 airplanes a month, will build up to this new level by increasing output to 1O airplanes a month by January 1997 and then to 12 airplanes a month by the second quarter of 1997.
Boeing said it also is developing plans and working with suppliers to ensure that it can respond to even greater demand for the 737 in the future.
